subject: Medico: residency & DR recovery follow-up
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medicohealth.com>; Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@medicohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Mar 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Medico: residency & DR recovery follow-up

Laura / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and so the engineering team has a clear set of follow-ups. I’ve attached a short controls summary and a pinning options matrix.

Call highlights (summary):
- Primary requirement: patient records and associated PII must be stored and processed only in EU zones.
- DR/failover: Medico is open to a US warm-standby for up to 72 hours during a declared disaster, provided encryption and access controls are enforced and audit trails are preserved.
- Logs & audits: access logs and redaction markers must be available to Medico for 5 years; security team will want S3-style immutable storage for audit exports.
- Classification: samples of payloads (PHI vs non-PHI) need confirmation — we need two representative payloads for our evals.

Action items we will take:
1) Ben to run a feasibility check for EU pin + US warm-standby (KV cache behavior, warm-warm vs cold standby implications).
2) Marcus to document logging retention and redaction/export paths and provide an ops playbook for audits.
3) Kimberly to draft a short SOW and proposed timeline for a pilot (attached SOW draft).

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the formal definition Medico is using for "patient-identifiable" vs "pseudonymized"? A short example JSON would be helpful.
- If the 72-hr DR window is acceptable, are there any legal constraints on cross-border transfer during that window?

Attachments: pii_controls_summary.pdf (overview), pinning-options-matrix.xlsx (technical tradeoffs).

Thanks — available for a quick technical follow-up Thurs 09:00 CET if that works.

— Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medicohealth.com>

Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@medicohealth.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Medico: residency & DR recovery follow-up

Kimberly — thanks for the recap and for the attachments. Quick clarifications from our side after circulating to legal and infrastructure: 

- Residency: yes, production patient records must remain in EU (Ireland primary region). We can permit system metadata and telemetry to be stored outside EU if redacted of identifiers.
- DR window: 72 hours is our current operational threshold. Legal has flagged that any transfer must be logged and require an emergency-authority sign-off (we'll provide the process).
- Logs retention: we require audit logs covering data access and administrative actions to be retained for 5 years; logs that include identifiers must be encrypted and we may request a monthly export to our archive.
- PII examples: attaching our internal requirements doc (medico_requirements.docx) with examples of identifiers and acceptable pseudonymization patterns.

Next steps from Medico:
- We'll provide two anonymized example payloads by EOD Friday that reflect your three common call flows.
- Please propose a concrete pilot timeline; ideally pilot starts within 3–4 weeks.

Thanks,
Laura

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Looping in engineering notes after a quick run with the runtime team. Quoting Laura below for context: 

> "Residency: production patient records must remain in EU (Ireland primary region). We can permit system metadata and telemetry to be stored outside EU if redacted of identifiers."

Technical notes: 
- Pinning approach: we can pin workloads to Ireland region nodes for both model inference and KV cache. Pinning means the KV cache and prefix cache are colocated with compute; cross-region read-through will be disabled by default.
- Warm standby design: maintain a hot-replica of model weights + daily state snapshot shipped to a US region with encrypted transfer (AES-256). In a DR event we can promote US warm-standby — this will incur a cold-cache penalty for ~1–2 minutes per endpoint while KV caches rebuild (we can pre-warm common prefixes).
- Logging & exports: we can provide an immutable export of audit logs to a Medico-controlled S3 in EU; logs that contain identifiers will be encrypted server-side and signed by customer KMS. We can support 5-year retention policy and monthly export automation.

Open technical questions for legal + infra:
- Do they require that encryption keys for backups in the US be EU-resident? If so, we need to plan KMS/HSM placement.
- For payload examples: do they include screenshots or free-text clinical notes (PHI) — that affects redaction approach.

Proposed next steps (technical):
1) Marcus to write a 1-page DR runbook describing failover criteria, sign-off flow, and rollback steps.
2) Ben to produce a cost delta estimate for maintaining EU pinned capacity + US warm-standby.
3) Schedule the pilot kickoff once Medico sends sample payloads.

— Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

I’ve attached a first-pass SOW (SOW_medico_draft_v1.pdf) for your review — it calls out scope, pilot success metrics (latency, correct pinning behavior, audit export verification), and preliminary timelines. Please annotate and return; we’ll bake legal redlines into the contract.

Thanks all — moving to action items.
